  • In a recent development, all three stocks have also tumbled.
  • In a recent development, but their businesses haven't followed the stocks down.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:43PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), Coherent (COHR -12.90%) and Dell Technologies (DELL -11.04%) all supply the same artificial intelligence (AI) build-out. Nvidia makes the chips, Coherent makes optical parts that carry data between them, and Dell builds the servers they go into.

In a recent development, all three stocks have also tumbled. Nvidia closed at a record $239.24 on Oct. 6 and trades around $153 as I write this, about 36% lower. Coherent, near $223, is off about 48% from its June 2 record close. And Dell, roughly $322, is about 45% under the $588.40 record close it set on Sept. 17.

In a recent development, but their businesses haven't followed the stocks down. Each organization's latest report reveals data center demand still growing, and I think each stock now leaves room for gains through 2030.

Sources indicate that on Nov. 11, Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO and made Colette Kress, the chief financial officer, interim CEO while it looks for a permanent one.

The business, though, kept speeding up. In the fiscal third quarter of 2027, which ended Oct. 25, 2026, Nvidia's data center revenue hit $107.6 billion. It was 21% above the previous quarter, and sequential growth accelerated from 18% in fiscal Q2. Management expects around $130 billion in total revenue for the fiscal fourth quarter, but that period has an extra week.

Shares still dropped about 3% the day after the Nov. 17 report. Using analysts' average forecast for fiscal 2028 (the year ending January 2028), the stock costs under 10 times earnings, while the forward price-to-earnings ratio of the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) is around 18.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Sources indicate that the CEO search might keep some investors wary for a while. But for a business whose data center sales more than doubled year over year, I think the stock is cheap.

Coherent's lasers and optical transceivers move data between chips inside a data center, and between data centers.

Industry observers note that showing how much AI now powers the company, Coherent's datacenter and communications segment took in $1.95 billion in its fiscal first quarter of 2027 (which ended Sept. 30, 2026), or 82% of total revenue. Segment sales rose 79% year over year and 21% sequentially, up from $1.09 billion a year before and $1.62 billion in fiscal Q4 2026.

Industry observers note that for a 2030 holder, the longer deals might matter more. Coherent signed one for its newly introduced PhotonLink optics platform worth around $20 billion over five years, with revenue starting to ramp in early 2028. Also, on Nov. 18 the board approved a share buyback program of up to $2 billion, around 5% of Coherent's market value at the current stock price.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Industry observers note that granted, operating cash flow was negative $93 million last quarter, and Coherent spent another $776 million on upcoming equipment and facilities to expand capacity. And at around 22 times earnings using analysts' fiscal 2027 forecasts (that year ends in June 2027), it's the priciest of the three. Still, with management expecting pro forma revenue growth (which leaves out businesses it sold) over 60% this fiscal year, I'd call that valuation reasonable.

Dell's AI server orders are arriving faster than Dell is shipping them. In its fiscal second quarter of 2027 (which ended July 31, 2026), the company booked a record $60.9 billion in AI server orders, almost four times the $16.4 billion in AI server revenue it recorded. It closed the period with a record $95 billion AI server backlog.

According to recent reports, total revenue rose 58% year over year to $47.0 billion. And with management guiding to non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share of $25.50 this fiscal year, the stock trades at around 13 times those earnings.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

But profits have outpaced cash. Dell's operating cash flow dropped 13% year over year to $2.2 billion in fiscal Q2, even as net income more than tripled to $4.1 billion. A big reason is financing receivables (money customers owe Dell under financing deals), which cut operating cash flow by around $6.7 billion in the quarter. The fiscal third-quarter report on Tuesday, Nov. 24, might show whether more of that cash is starting to come in.

All three stocks might continue to slide together if AI spending cools. But each organization is growing fast, and I think each trades at a valuation that leaves room for that growth to reach shareholders by 2030.

In a recent development, I'd start with Nvidia, the cheapest of the three relative to its expected earnings and the one whose data center growth accelerated last quarter. Coherent would be next, with its multiyear PhotonLink deal. Dell is worth a look too, but I'd keep the position smaller until its cash flow catches up to its profits.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oura developed a tool for its frequent-flying members that could help them stave off the worst of jet lag.

Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, on Tuesday, Oura announced Jet Lag Strategy, a fresh feature designed to help travelers feel alert and energized after crossing several time zones.

Also: Oura Ring owners may get in-app access to real doctors soon – what we know.

Jet Lag Plan takes into account your travel itinerary, sleep patterns, and body responses to provide guidance for traveling members entering new time zones.

Jet lag happens when circadian rhythms are at odds with local time zones, but there are a few things people can do to adjust.

Oura factors in the direction of travel, how many time zones are crossed, individual light windows, and sleep timing.

Ring users will enter their flight details, including information like multi-stop trips, and also include the reason for the trip. Oura adjusts the Jet Lag Proposal accordingly, and a business trip’s plan may differ in intensity from that of a vacation.

According to recent reports, “Two people on the same flight can get different looks, because guidance reflects your itinerary, your typical sleep schedule, and your chronotype,” Oura writes in a blog post. The chronotype refers to Oura’s sleep chronotype, which categorizes people into six types (early morning, morning, early evening, and so on) based on their historical sleep activity.

Also: I wore the Oura Ring 5 for a month.

After adding these details, Oura provides each user with timely guidance throughout their trip. This guidance could include recommendations on when to begin or end caffeine consumption or light exposure, and when to start preparing for sleep. The plan is designed for those crossing three or more time zones. Members can follow along with these recommendations by checking them off as they complete each one. Users can also talk to Oura’s Advisor in the event of flight or timing changes.

Jet Lag Proposal is now available for Oura Members with Oura Ring Gen 3 or later.

Go to your home screen, tap the + and select Jet Lag Proposal to get started. You can also tell Oura Advisor about a trip to initiate Jet Lag Plan. If the Oura app detects a time zone shift of 3 or more hours, Jet Lag Plan may appear as a push notification.

Also: Why your USB-C cables look alike, but work differently – and how to tell them apart.

It has been revealed that on Apple’s side, any iPhone in the US running iOS 27 with a T-Mobile or Verizon-provided eSIM can use iPhone Handoff. AT&T does not currently support iPhone Handoff.

However, the code strings uncovered by Android Authority show that Android’s Fast Switch will work similarly to iPhone Handoff, in that owners must be signed in to both devices under the same Google account for the feature to work.

Strings in Google’s SIM Manager app also point to no sharing between two customers, so this feature isn’t a way to circumvent carrier fees by adding service to someone else’s phone for the price of one.

It has been revealed that if Fast Switch works anything like iPhone Handoff, which it appears it will, one eSIM can be switched between two phones. So, calls, messages, location services, and other information synced to your Apple ID can remain consistent between two devices.

Also: 5 hidden iOS 27 features that make older iPhones better.

Some third-party apps, like banking, communications, or social media, may also remain consistent across the two phones, depending on the app’s syncing behavior.

Features like Apple’s iPhone Handoff and Google’s Fast Switch are ideal for people who regularly use two phones. Business owners and digital creators may want one phone strictly for business purposes and the other for personal use.

Also: Google Wallet turns your Android phone into a digital house key.

It has been revealed that in that case, one person can keep up with two phones without paying for two phone service lines through their carrier. Still, customers will incur a fee, as T-Mobile charges $5/month for iPhone Handoff, while Verizon charges $10/month.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that have you been using the fresh Siri AI?
  • Also: 5 apps I need Siri AI to work with now that it’s open to third-party developers.
  • Industry observers note that apple hasn’t been shy about stating that the use of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence for specific tasks would face daily access limits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that have you been using the fresh Siri AI? If so, how much? I’ve been turning to it a lot since the release of iOS 27. Well, how we use it — and how often — will soon depend on how much we pay for an iCloud+ plan.

Also: 5 apps I need Siri AI to work with now that it’s open to third-party developers.

Industry observers note that apple hasn’t been shy about stating that the use of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence for specific tasks would face daily access limits. Increased limits would be granted based on your iCloud+ subscription. Now the tech giant has revealed how much it will cost you and when the limits will begin.

Recent findings suggest that “Starting with the 2027 software releases, Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for owners with a supported device set to a supported language,” Apple mentioned on a support page updated November 16. “Some features rely on powerful server models and have limits where increased access is available with eligible iCloud+ aims, starting with the 27.3 release.”.

iOS 27.3 is expected to launch in early December, so that’s when the daily usage limits will kick in.

At that point, people with no paid iCloud+ blueprint and even those with the $0.99-per-month 50 GB plan will be the most limited, with Apple saying only that they’ll face a “Standard Device Limit.”.

Industry observers note that what is a standard limit? That depends not just on how many times you tap into Siri per day but on what tasks you assign it. Basic Siri commands, such as setting timers and alarms or sending standard text messages, will remain free and unlimited.

Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

Advanced Siri and Apple Intelligence tasks will bump into the usage limits. These include the following, according to Apple:.

Recent findings suggest that one positive here is that the limits are per device not per account. That means you can use Siri AI and Apple Intelligence with the same account across your iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Vision Pro without fear of chewing up too much of your quota.

This all sounds like a way for Apple to steer people to more expensive iCloud+ accounts. But the limits are in place for a key reason. Basic commands are processed on your device, so they don’t require the use of Apple servers. More advanced tasks are processed using server-side AI models, which can feel the strain if too many people access them all at once.

Also: What you’ll pay for AI agents will be wildly variable and unpredictable.

How will you know if you use up your daily allotment and what happens then? You’ll receive a notification if you hit your limit for a particular feature category. At that point, you can still give Siri basic tasks to perform. But advanced ones will be paused until your limit resets the next day. Otherwise, Apple is undoubtedly hoping that people who continually run into limits will upgrade to a pricier iCloud+ plan.

Our Readers Say This Is the Laptop Brand to Shop for During Black Friday Sales

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, holiday sales like Black Friday and Cyber Monday usually have good personal tech deals on TVs, wearables and robot vacuums.
  • It has been revealed that we recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to get their opinion on their laptop brand — including their take on its battery life, durability and performance for gaming and graphics.
  • Recent findings suggest that apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple consumers saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, holiday sales like Black Friday and Cyber Monday usually have good personal tech deals on TVs, wearables and robot vacuums. It’s also a good time to shop for a latest laptop, but not every brand is worth your time and money.

It has been revealed that we recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to get their opinion on their laptop brand — including their take on its battery life, durability and performance for gaming and graphics. Our readers could choose from many popular laptop brands, but one was a clear favorite. It claimed eight awards, including the overall winner for CNET’s People’s Pick award. And it’s the one worth heavily considering if you plan to buy a new laptop while there are holiday savings.

Recent findings suggest that apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple consumers saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop. In comparison, 22.5% say they’re satisfied — bringing Apple to a near-perfect overall satisfaction score of 96.7%.

Apple’s overall impression also speaks to other awards it wins from CNET readers, including high ratings for its impressive battery life, display quality and high-quality build. All of those categories and more sum up Apple’s brand loyalty nod, with 68% of MacBook owners saying they would buy the same laptop and model from Apple again.

Recent findings suggest that how much are people paying for MacBooks? CNET found that 43.5% of Apple users paid at least $1,500. Until earlier in 2026, the MacBook Air was Apple’s entry-level laptop, priced at least $1,299. The introduction of the budget-friendly MacBook Neo brought that down to a more reasonable $699. However, despite Apple’s laptops being more expensive than those from other brands, they still ranked high for their value proposition. Part of the reason for that is that MacBooks received high marks for hardware reliability. “Apple’s MacBooks might cost more than the average laptop, but their premium build quality means they’re built for the long haul,” said Matt Elliott, CNET’s laptop editor.

Recent findings suggest that if you strategy to have your laptop for a while, you may be impressed by other features that make work easier and faster, like its M-series central processing unit for task management and AI capabilities, great battery life and a one-of-a-kind operating system — currently MacOS 27. All of the features and specifications bundled together make Apple’s perception as a high-end laptop worth the investment for long-term satisfaction.

It has been revealed that apple clinches a near-perfect score for its value perception. According to our survey results, 44% of Apple users mentioned their MacBook has exceptional value. Others say their MacBook is worth what they paid for it (50.9%) — for a total positive score of 94.6%.

Industry observers note that digging deeper into Apple’s cost-to-value rating, 81.8% of Apple owners paid at least $1,000 for their laptops, which may seem costly, but Apple people seem OK with the price. That could be because, even though Apple has only three laptop models in a handful of sizes in its lineup, each one delivers solid performance and storage.

In a recent development, take Apple’s proprietary processing chips, for example — each upgrade since the M1 release has improved the laptop’s speed, battery life and performance. Now the M6 can handle the MacBook’s AI capabilities, storage and high-resolution graphics. And for all of that power, most MacBooks are relatively thin and lightweight, making them easier for mobility — just a few of the reasons Apple customers may be OK with paying more for what they’re getting.

According to recent reports, battery life is a major deal for many laptop buyers, and that’s another area where Apple delivers. Over a quarter of those surveyed (25.7%) said their MacBook’s battery life exceeds 10 hours — which is more than enough for a full day of work in most cases. And 18.7% say their MacBook’s battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours — totaling 44.4% of MacBook users saying their battery lasts 8 hours or more.

Comparatively, non-Apple laptop brands fall short in this category. Only 16.4% of Lenovo users say their laptop’s battery lasts at least 8 hours, and even fewer for Dell (12.7%) and HP (11.8%). If you’re leaning toward a MacBook for its battery life, CNET’s lab test indicates that the MacBook Neo lasts 13 hours and 26 minutes for online streaming, whereas the Apple MacBook Air 13-inch M5 (2026 model) lasts 17 hours and 2 minutes.

Apple sweeps the brightness, color accuracy and clarity category with 99.2% of its users either satisfied or extremely satisfied with their laptop’s screen performance. No Apple users reported dissatisfaction.

Recent findings suggest that “Apple has long been a favorite for creative professionals and content creators for good reason: Its MacBook displays are some of the best you’ll find on any laptop,” mentioned Josh Goldman, CNET’s managing editor for computers. “While Apple may use marketing names like Retina and Liquid Retina to describe display features, they do translate into sharp and clear text and images, with excellent brightness, contrast, color gamut coverage and color accuracy.”.

Recent findings suggest that the latest MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR even goes beyond what MacBook users have come to expect. It’s Apple’s first OLED touchscreen laptop and features next-level brightness, color and contrast.

Apple receives high ratings: 80% of MacBook owners say it has premium build quality, 18.2% say it’s solid, and those results don’t surprise us.

And MacBooks seem durable and reliable, with 87% of Apple people reporting no hardware failures on their MacBooks, while 8% say minor software fixes resolved their challenges. Only 3% needed minor hardware repairs, and 2.2% needed major repairs — which could be fixes such as a battery or screen replacement.

Our editors say the M5 MacBook Air is thin and lightweight, but still has a well-built aluminum design. And the M5 Pro MacBook Pro is sturdy, too. What sets Apple’s laptop hardware apart could be its aluminum chassis — the casing that holds all of the components together.

“Apple makes three lines of MacBooks — the Neo, Air and Pro — and focuses on making those the best they can possibly be. They are all built to deliver a premium experience using high-quality materials, and that even includes the entry-level MacBook Neo,” stated Goldman.

Lastly, Apple uses durable materials, such as the 100% recycled aluminum alloy it says encloses the 14-inch MacBook Pro. And the tech giant has several testing facilities to test MacBook durability.

Sources indicate that when it comes to getting your daily tasks done, most CNET readers with MacBooks (70.9%) say Apple’s laptops handle workloads flawlessly. It’s worth noting that 45% use their MacBook for work tasks, but no Apple owners reported poor performance.

Sources indicate that here’s why that might be: Apple’s laptops are packed with top-notch performance specs and features, like their powerful processors, unified memory and fast storage. Better processor performance means enhanced graphics, on-device AI capabilities and faster task speeds, all of which add up to being able to finish work, play games or stream videos without issues or lags caused by your laptop’s hardware.

On the software side, MacOS 27 Golden Gate gives you built-in AI features, like Siri AI and Visual Intelligence. And you can organize your Safari tabs by topic and use the Notify Me tool to be notified of website changes, like price drops or breaking news. Plus, you can create shortcuts to automate tasks. Coupling all of these features and specifications explains why Apple people rate MacBooks so highly for getting the job done.

Industry observers note that apple leads the way on brand retention with 68% of Apple users planning to buy the same MacBook model again, while 29.1% would buy another model from Apple’s lineup. Only 3% would switch to another brand that’s not Apple.

Usually, when you buy one Apple product, you’re likely to stick to the brand’s ecosystem, especially since Apple has its own operating systems to access its unique features and work seamlessly with other Apple products with Apple’s Continuity feature. For example, you can start an email on your iPhone, but finish typing it on your MacBook. Or you can call or send a text from your laptop without reaching for your iPhone. Other features work across Apple devices, including iCloud, Universal Clipboard and AirDrop.

Asus wins as a midtier laptop choice with 67% of Asus owners paying between $500 and $1,499. There’s a sweet spot in this range with 38% spending between $500 and $999, and 28% paying between $1,000 and $1,499.

If you’re planning to spend that amount on a new laptop, you may also be pleased to know that Asus earns a higher satisfaction rating compared with other non-Apple laptop brands — 48% of Asus owners say they’re extremely satisfied.

According to recent reports, asus laptops have a few features and specifications that may speak to that rating, regardless of budget. For example, the Zenbook A14 has a thin, lightweight design that’s rigid, with long battery life and an OLED display with strong contrast and color performance. This Copilot Plus PC sells for $1,600 (but retailers like Best Buy regularly have it on sale for less). Comparatively, these premium features from other brands could cost more or sacrifice notable must-have features for the price.

Asus has other laptops worth exploring depending on your needs, like the budget-friendly Asus ZenBook S 14 or the premium Asus ROG Zephyrus G14 that could be good for gamers and creators.

Over one-third of Acer laptop owners (38%) paid less than $500 for their laptop — which is greater than other laptop brands in this price range. Yet, 44% of Acer users say their laptop has exceptional value, while 50% say the value is fair — bringing a total positive cost-to-value score of over 94%. Acer also has an overall satisfaction score of 92.6% — the highest of non-Apple laptop brands.

If you’re impressed by Acer’s value and satisfaction scores, there are a few budget-friendly Acer options to consider. The Acer Aspire 16 AI wins CNET’s Editors’ Choice award. It has a massive 16-inch screen but is still lightweight (3.5 pounds). And it has good battery life (over 21 hours on CNET’s battery drain test). There are a few other pluses, like the 1440p web camera that may be good for video conferencing and a sizable touchpad. All of those features and more add up to $700, which could make it a good computer for work or casual browsing. If you’re looking to spend slightly less, its predecessor, the Aspire 14 AI, is originally $639, but you may be able to score deals on both models during holiday sales.

In a recent development, even though Apple is highly recommended by CNET readers, there are plenty of other laptop models and brands worth considering depending on your needs. Here are a few non-Apple laptop brands that are runner-ups to CNET’s People’s Picks winners that you shouldn’t count out of your laptop search.

Recent findings suggest that lenovo is best known for packing a powerful laptop into a compact design with tablet functionality, like its Yoga line, and its durable ThinkPad business models. But CNET readers with Lenovo laptops say the brand’s battery life stands out most compared with other non-MacBook laptops.

In a recent development, survey findings show that 16% of Lenovo owners say their laptops can run for 8 hours or more. And 10.5% say their laptop battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours, while 6% say their Lenovo laptops can withstand at least 10 hours before needing a charge. That’s more than what readers say about other non-Apple brands. The Yoga 9i 2-in-1 Aura Edition lasts 25 hours and 45 minutes — making it one of the best laptop batteries CNET experts have tested.

Sources indicate that goldman noted Lenovo has such a large and varied PC selection using the latest chips from Intel, AMD, Qualcomm and Nvidia that there is something for everyone and every budget. Even those who spend less on a Lenovo laptop can expect solid performance, including battery life.

If your laptop’s hardware fails or it breaks, you may be in the market for a latest laptop sooner than expected. Think about cooling fan problems, overheating or your laptop not powering on at all. Over half (68%) of Lenovo laptop owners said they haven’t had any hardware challenges with their laptops — the most compared to other non-MacBooks.

Industry observers note that beyond hardware durability, Lenovo also scores highly for its build and construction — overall making it a sturdy laptop choice. In our survey, 38% of Lenovo laptop owners say their laptop has a premium feel, while 51% say it’s solid — totaling a positive score of 89%.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking for recommendations, the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 has an all-metal design. And the Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 is a business laptop with Lenovo’s well-known X1 Carbon exterior and new Space Frame design, which Elliott says makes it easier to repair or replace parts if needed.

In a recent development, many Lenovo laptop people are loyal to the brand, which speaks to the overall positive satisfaction rating of 83%. If Lenovo owners were in the market for a latest laptop, nearly three in four (73.2%) say they would buy another Lenovo laptop. Breaking down the percentage, 33.6% say they would buy the same model again. Meanwhile, 39.6% would buy a different model but stick to Lenovo.

Here’s why that might be. Lenovo offers a plethora of options to choose from based on your needs — while still evolving its laptops. For instance, the Lenovo Legion 5i Gen 10 has an open M.2 slot for a second storage drive and an OLED screen for crisp, colorful images — making it perfect for gaming. Its Yoga two-in-ones let you seamlessly switch between a tablet and traditional laptop, while Lenovo’s ThinkPad and ThinkBook business laptops offer everything from ultralight 2-pound bodies to expanding rollable screens. And its upcoming designs don’t sacrifice the must-have needs like long battery life, durability and chip efficiency that lend to strong performance.

It has been revealed that asus wins over nearly half of its laptop owners, with 47.5% giving it an exceptional value rating  — exceeding expectations for its price. Take our Editors’ Choice pick, the Asus Zenbook A14. It’s super thin and lightweight, but it’s still sturdy thanks to its Ceralumnium body. Plus, it has supreme 24-hour battery life, 1TB of storage and an OLED display — all for $1,200. While that’s more expensive than some laptops, it’s what’s included in that price that makes it worthwhile compared with other non-Apple laptop brands.

In a recent development, asus is the top non-Apple laptop option to consider for tasks, with 47.7% of CNET readers giving it high ratings. That’s followed by 40.4% of Asus laptop owners who say it has very good task performance. When it comes to tasks, 37% primarily use their Asus laptops for work, while 5% use theirs for gaming.

Industry observers note that asus is well known for having lightweight laptops with all-day-and-night battery life and stunning display quality. Asus laptops like the Asus ROG Zephyrus G16 have a good port selection, which could be good for gaming, work or simply connecting different devices without the need for additional adapters. And the Asus Zenbook S 14 has a strong neural processing unit that contributes to its high-speed AI performance.

Asus scores highest for its screen brightness and clarity, with over half (51%) extremely satisfied with its screen quality and brightness, while 38.6% say they’re satisfied, giving Asus an overall satisfaction rate of 90%. One common thread we noticed in Asus laptops is their OLED screens, which deliver high-resolution video and graphics. Asus laptops also combine stunning display quality with excellent performance and at surprisingly low prices for all of their features.

For example, the Asus Zenbook 14 isn’t the highest-quality OLED we’ve seen, but it still produces clear text and graphics on a 14-inch screen, along with exceptional black levels, Elliott remarked. That’s still better than LCDs that many other non-MacBooks have, and could be the reason Asus owners rate it so highly in this category.

Sources indicate that dell wins our readers over as a top choice for high-end laptops. One-third (33.3%) of Dell owners spent over $1,500, and of that percentage, 15.2% spent over $2,000.

Recent findings suggest that dell’s premium laptops largely cater to business and gaming with their standout features and performance. The Alienware 16X Aurora is Dell’s midrange gaming laptop with user-replaceable RAM, a bright display and strong performance for $2,280. But if you want more gaming features, Dell has the Alienware 16 Area-51, which has even better gaming performance, upgradable RAM and three SSD slots for $2,530. And if you’re looking for a non-Mac alternative that comes close to MacBook quality and performance, the higher-end Dell XPS 14 is the one to choose. It has the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H CPU, Intel Arc B390 graphics and 1TB of storage for $1,950.

Recent findings suggest that CNET commissioned Alchemer to conduct the People’s Picks survey to compile data. The survey was carried out online, and all figures are from Alchemer. The total sample comprised 1,003 adults. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus). Fieldwork was undertaken from Sept. 1 to Oct. 10, 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Gemini can now turn your notes and other sources in your Gemini Notebook (previously called NotebookLM) into interactive pages or sites to help you better process complicated information.

Complete with flashcards, dashboards, and colorful panels, the sites make it easier to study and understand intricate concepts. I tested the feature, confirmed Tuesday, to see how efficient it is at creating a navigable site that is actually helpful and stays loyal to sources.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s new Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector in my tests.

Sources indicate that because Notebooks are built with the sources you provide, like textbooks, files, or notes, the sites are created with the data that is in your Gemini Notebook. Notebook has three tabs: Sources, Chat, and Studio. The site option is in the Studio tab, listed under what you can create.

If you’re taking a college class, you could put all the information you need to prepare for a test and use the interactive site as a study guide that you can share with others.

To test this, I gave Notebook the following prompt:.

“Make me a site that visually explains how cellular respiration works, breaking down each stage with interactive diagrams and self-check flashcards.”.

Since I’m not in a class that would give me those study materials, I gave Gemini online sources to use for this. Gemini cited the sources in my notebook, then spent a few minutes creating the interactive site. Gemini will give you a quick update when it’s done, including a summary of the source information as it pertains to your request and instructions on where to find the site.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours.

As promised, my cellular respiration notes were complete and organized on an interactive, visually appealing site that was easy to navigate. The coolest feature on the site was the flashcards, which you can hover over to see which ones you’ve studied.

The interactive site feature is now available to Gemini Notebook consumers and will soon come to the mobile app. As someone who knows very little about coding, I was pretty satisfied to see the information Gemini put together presented in explorable, easy-to-understand tabs on a site.

Apple’s Support Community Shuts Down on Friday, Removing User Discussions

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (901 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations.
  • Industry observers note that A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov.
  • According to recent reports, apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac issues as early as 1998.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations. For a few more hours, the website will remain read-only, but I’ve found the search function crashes intermittently, so even that ability isn’t very reliable.

Industry observers note that A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov. 10, warning visitors that the site would shut down and be offline entirely on Friday. If you want to look up a specific Apple troubleshooting topic on iPhones or HomePods, you should do it this evening. Soon, the entire peer advice and support site, which has been operating for nearly three decades, will be gone.

According to recent reports, apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac issues as early as 1998. For those of you who might remember, that’s the year Apple debuted its iMac G3, the desktop with a translucent blue teardrop-shaped case. The iMac G3 abandoned legacy ports and the floppy disc drive in favor of CD-ROM and USB.

Back then, the site was called Apple Tech Exchange, later renamed Apple Discussions until it eventually became the Apple Support Community in 2011. Many still turned to forums for DIY solutions, using it to get advice from other tinkerers interested in figuring out how to fix things on their own.

An Apple spokesperson told CNET the decision was made “after careful evaluation of our strategy and our customers’ needs.” Apple’s site notification directs people to visit the official Apple Support site. You’ll also be able to use Apple’s online chat, support phone numbers and in-store support, the same way they worked in the past.

Recent findings suggest that apple is one of the first American tech companies to give up its community discussion site — Google still has Google Communities Help, and Amazon manages its own forum domain with discussions from both staff and people. But Apple’s sudden closure could indicate a major shift, with others eventually following suit. It has highlighted an ongoing discussion about the role of peer support in tech, how AI has changed our online conversations and more.

When news of the shutdown spread, Apple consumers flocked to the internet to express everything from dismay to vindication.

For many, the Apple Support Community forums were controversial, not least because it wasn’t always clear how they worked. The site contained “user-submitted content, comments and opinions” and was “for informational purposes only,” yet many would mistake it for official Apple Support from staff.

In discussions on Reddit about the closure, many bemoaned the absence of real Apple employees from the site’s forums and found the advice from other Support Community owners to often be frustrating and not worth the effort. On the unofficial Apple subreddit, many mourned the loss of community while also noting that answers on the forum were often much harder to come by. Others said the site grew less helpful over the years.

CNET phone reviewer and senior editor Mike Sorrentino told me that the forum shutdown “will likely drive customers looking for help with basic questions to Apple’s official support articles rather than user-created threads.” But Sorrentino also acknowledged that the move reflects a general trend away from the site, with more people getting answers from sites like Reddit. “Apple’s always been big on controlling what information is shown on its website, and in that view, moving away from user discussion makes sense,” he said.

Just this week, I used the Apple Support Community site when looking for an answer to a problem implementing Apple Intelligence on my home security cameras, which required jumping through multiple hoops. Perhaps tellingly, I ended up finding the correct answer on Reddit. But that could become harder to do in the near future.

Industry observers note that the shutdown of Apple’s peer support forums is definitely a sign of the times, especially as tech companies push people away from repairing their own devices and toward replacing them outright — or at least encourage device owners to pay for official support services. It’s also a sign of the growing role of artificial intelligence, which is capitalizing on user-created content to provide summaries, moving people away from organic discussion and exchange on sites like these.

Reddit has lucrative data-licensing contracts with Google and OpenAI, allowing the companies to train their AI models on Reddit’s massive archive of human discussions, as well as surface Reddit content in tools like Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT. Reddit is also moving to a login-only viewing mode, making it significantly harder for casual customers to find answers unless they trust AI summaries.

Apple may be leery of keeping so much user knowledge online for AI models to scrape for their own answers. The organization may also want to prevent AI summaries from providing information from past forum users on how to jailbreak Apple devices or DIY fixes, even as the EU has mandated that Apple start building replaceable batteries by next year. And it wouldn’t be a good look if Siri AI started regurgitating incorrect or outdated info it had picked up from Apple’s own sites.

Whatever the reason, the circle of Apple users helping users has grown smaller, and that doesn’t bode well for support forums as a whole. It may be time to start archiving those years of data before other tech companies implement similar plans.

Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI model training – here’s how

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI.
  • Also: I checked Gemini’s latest Memory summary to see what it knew about me.
  • In a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI. But for people with privacy concerns, the only way to opt out of this was to delete your entire chat history. Now, Google is overhauling the process to eliminate that drawback.

Also: I checked Gemini’s latest Memory summary to see what it knew about me.

In a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road.

Currently, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two.

To correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two new settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

“With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google noted in an announcement shared to Gemini users via email.

Industry observers note that here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both new settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats.

It has been revealed that almost all AIs include a setting for model training that you typically have to manually disable if you’re concerned about your privacy. But most let you opt out without turning off your chat history.

Recent findings suggest that chatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.”.

Also: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027.

Sources indicate that in all those cases, you still retain access to your conversation history. In contrast, Google has been the only AI player among the majors to impose a restriction for those who want to opt out of AI training. Based on past actions, Google has often earned a reputation for being privacy-unfriendly. I’m glad to see the organization take this step in the right direction.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Monday, Google rolled out an M157 enhancement for the Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, with a handful of new features and performance boosts to streamline your workflow and browsing experience.

While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.

Industry observers note that also: Googlebooks? The best laptop for Android customers is something else.

Here are the five new Chrome features on Googlebook OS to know about.

If you’ve ever had to share your screen on a video call, you know how irritating it can be to switch tabs without having to repeatedly start and stop sharing. This Chrome upgrade adds a tab-sharing controls bar; when you share a browser tab in a video call, Chrome will display a persistent control bar at the top of the window so you can “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

Also: 6 Chrome default settings I changed to instantly.

According to recent reports, when you hover over a collapsed vertical tab rail with your mouse or trackpad, it will expand, so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups. The rail will collapse again when you move the cursor away.

In a recent development, this auto-expand feature is enabled by default. If you want to turn it off or on, go to Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover,” or right-click the vertical tab rail.

The Chrome update allows you to manually resize your vertical tab bar to view longer page titles when needed. The browser will remember your custom tab width, even after you open a latest window or restart the browser. (You’ll just need to turn “Auto expand tabs on hover” off for it to work.).

You can now save individual Chrome Settings subpages as direct web addresses that you can type, bookmark, or link to directly (for example, chrome://settings/privacy), meaning you won’t have to go digging around in menus to change your preferences anymore. You can navigate between these Settings subpages with the Back and Forward buttons.

According to recent reports, the system’s “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for menu save actions, such as “Save link as” and “Save image as,” so you can more easily rename files and select a destination folder. This includes Google Drive or external storage.

Recent findings suggest that also: Google Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast.

Outside of these fresh features, a few of Chrome M157’s performance fixes include the ability to press Ctrl+L to reveal and select web addresses; keeping your bookmarks bar visible in fullscreen mode and while screen sharing; better media controls while using Picture-in-Picture mode; and the ability to partially translate PDFs within your browser.

If you have Chrome set up to automatically download and install updates, you won’t have to lift a finger to take advantage of the new features and performance boosts.

But if you’ve disabled automatic updates, you can manually enhancement by selecting the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of your Chrome window and navigating to Help > About Google Chrome > Relaunch.

Also: My week with new Googlebooks: The good, the bad, and the promising.

If the Relaunch option is greyed out or nowhere to be found, you’re running on the latest version of Chrome. And if you were working on something before the patch, don’t worry: Chrome will save your open tabs and reopen them automatically when you restart.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov.
  • Google has announced that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini.
  • To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov. 17, 2026, and it’s carrying over features that let you share Skills and add files from Google products.

Google has announced that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini. Any Gems you have created will automatically convert, but you can transfer them manually if you want to start using them now.

To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.

While the Gemini Gems feature is technically going away, any Gems you’ve created aren’t.

It has been revealed that if you access the Gems portion of Gemini (since the feature is on the way out, you now have to access this through Settings), you’ll see a message that claims “Starting November 17, 2026, we’ll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills.” (The cutoff date for accessing your Gems will be Dec. 16, 2026. Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit accounts will get cut off in March 2027, and Workspace education accounts will be cut off in June 2027.).

A Gemini Skill functions much the same as a Gem. You describe specific situations when Gemini should use the Skill automatically and tell Gemini what you want the Skill to do (it’s best to give specific examples of output). Google gives the example of a marketing team sharing a brand-voice skill that references their brand guidelines doc in Drive, or a team lead sharing an onboarding skill based on the team handbook.

The biggest difference is that Gems were standalone chats, while Skills are custom instructions that work in any conversation.

You can create as many Skills as you want, but only 100 can be active at a time.

To get consumers familiar with Skills, Google is bringing over two features from Gems.

Recent findings suggest that first, you can now share any Skill with other owners. When you share a Skill, you can choose whether the other person has permission to edit or view only. To share a Skill, go to the three-bar menu in the top left > Customize > Skills. You can view or change permissions from that screen.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours.

In a recent development, when a Skill is added, Gemini can use it automatically, or you can @mention it in chat to trigger it. One small caveat, though: you can only share Skills through the Gemini web app at the moment, not the mobile app.

Additionally, when you’re creating a Gemini Skill, you can choose to include files of up to 100MB from other Google products like Drive, Photos, and Notebook, along with files from your local device. Gemini will reference these files every time the Skill runs and upgrade in real time, Google indicates. These features existed with Gems; Google is just moving them to Skills to make the new feature more comparable.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that the pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin.
  • In a recent development, on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids. Uber Kids will cater to youngsters ages 10 to 12, those awkward years before adolescence. The latest program expands on the company’s other offering to underage passengers, Uber Teens, which launched in 2023 and provides rides to teenagers ages 13 to 17 in select cities.

Industry observers note that the pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin. Its expansion will depend on how well it performs in those regions. If successful, Uber Kids could bring a whole new influx of customers to the app, specifically parents and families needing help getting their kids from point A to point B.

In a recent development, on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger. But it seems like Uber took those concerns into account. The rideshare app has added a slew of mandatory requirements for both approved guardians and qualified drivers.

It has been revealed that first off, kids won’t simply be able to order a ride for themselves. The adult user must add the child to their family profile and complete an onboarding session covering the service’s safety features. They’ll also need to set up PIN verification for every trip. The parent or guardian must be present at the pickup location and provide the driver with a note containing the drop-off instructions.

As any parent would likely wonder (myself included), what about the drivers? How are they vetted?

Industry observers note that according to Uber, only the highest-rated drivers will be invited to take part in the program. They’ll need to pass thorough background checks and successfully complete an Uber Kids education curriculum. Moreover, they must agree to use live video streaming in their cars so that parents and guardians can watch the trip every step of the way.

In a recent development, live videos of underage passengers bring up a bunch of potential red flags, but Uber states all recordings will be encrypted, and no driver will have access to the content. Furthermore, sensors and GPS data will track the ride if the trip is interrupted or veers off course.

In a recent development, uber could face a tough time recruiting drivers for Uber Kids. Transporting minors adds extra responsibility and requires specific skills that many drivers may want to avoid. To sweeten the deal, Uber is offering eligible drivers a $20 bonus on their first ride and an extra $7 per trip after that.

An Uber spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that at today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the company introduced two newly introduced frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks.
  • Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model highlights 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.
  • Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that at today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the company introduced two newly introduced frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks. But there’s a bigger story: what these models might mean for Microsoft’s AI costs and its dependence on OpenAI.

Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model highlights 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Microsoft says MAI Code 2 offers comparable performance to GPT-6.1 Sol or Opus 5.5 at a fraction of the cost. Microsoft’s Code 2 Flash model is comparable to the lower-end GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, also at considerably lower cost.

Recent findings suggest that this doesn’t mean that those of us who pay for $100/month subscriptions will suddenly get the equivalent for five bucks. Instead, these are usage-based metrics based on API usage.

It has been revealed that it’s also vital to understand that the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests.

In a recent development, throughout Satya Nadella’s keynote, Microsoft revealed slides referencing a wide range of foundation models that are intended to work with Copilot and other Microsoft offerings. Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023, and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property.

But now, Redmond is benchmarking its internally built models against Anthropic and OpenAI offerings, and also touting that it’s integrating these new models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365, and Fabric.

Also: 75% of developers I surveyed prefer Claude Code over Codex.

One thing that Nadella made clear in today’s keynote is how central AI is becoming in everything Microsoft does. Nearly all of those AI operations previously involved the company paying some token fees back to the frontier model providers or customers doing the same thing.

But with high-performing models of its own, Microsoft may become substantially less dependent on outside model providers, especially for the incredible volume of fairly basic and routine AI requests that occur across the organization’s vast product line.

Sources indicate that if you think back over the history of agentic work models like ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork, you may recall that they originated as agentic coding tools. As users adopted the coding harnesses in Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to off-label productivity applications, the AI companies noticed and packaged work-centric agentic tools that were more non-programmer-friendly.

Also: I let ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork loose on my files – only one made me nervous.

There’s a lot of similarity between a coding agent and a work agent, including understanding a complex environment, using tools to change things, and producing reliable results. Coding turns out to be a very good environment for developing and testing these capabilities, particularly because code output is highly measurable. Coding agents are effective training grounds for non-coding work agents.

This becomes really interesting in today’s announcement. Along with Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, Microsoft declared MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash. Work Flash can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, track decisions and extract useful information from Teams, and more.

Industry observers note that think about the level of intelligence these tasks are demanding from the AI models. Not that much. As long as the models are good enough, they’ll be good enough.

If Microsoft can reduce its expenses and use reliable models at a much lower price, the organization itself will be able to save quite a bit of money across its entire software economy, while at the same time maintaining a deeper level of vertical integration and, therefore, control.

Let’s run some hypothetical numbers. Let’s say a organization is spending $0.01 per AI request, which, with these latest models, can drop down to $0.001 per request.

It has been revealed that also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer very carefully first.

A firm with a daily inference cost of a million dollars (a company like Microsoft, for example) could drop that daily cost to about $100,000. Add that up across a year, and the change in models could save $325 million annually.

A million here, a million there. Pretty soon, you’re talking real money.

In a recent development, there’s no direct evidence that Microsoft is trying to produce replacement models for the frontier providers’ offerings. But it is an interesting and compelling story if we look at Microsoft developing its own engines for the software it sells.

Sources indicate that microsoft says the numbers it’s reporting at are using a 50% introductory discount. That’s why I measured against $0.001 per request instead of $0.0005 per request above.

Benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The numbers are impressive. But as we all know, there are lies, damned lies, and benchmark results. I’m fairly sure Microsoft isn’t padding these numbers too much, because it benefits from the new models more than even its own customers, but still. It’s an open issue.

The manufacturer also described clearly that these latest models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads. You’re probably not going to use them to solve a decades-old mathematics challenge. But you’re very likely to use them to reformat your PowerPoint.

Speaking of reformatting your PowerPoint, Microsoft also emphasized that these new models did unusually well on visualization assignments. That’s a very good fit for not only UI design challenges but also graphics and slide production.

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1170 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

11 Steps I Use for Quick Smart Home Prep for Guests and Holiday Visitors

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1170 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As smart home and home security devices become more common, we’ve all got more devices around our homes when guests come over.
  • If you have holiday or event looks involving guests, especially guests staying over a day or two, I highly suggest making these adjustments to your smart home devices.
  • Read more: The 7 Most Common Home Security Mistakes to Stop Making.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As smart home and home security devices become more common, we’ve all got more devices around our homes when guests come over. Since I test home security and multiple smart devices, I tend to have a lot. But they don’t have to be a distraction when you have visitors staying over. On the contrary, smart tech can usually help out.

If you have holiday or event looks involving guests, especially guests staying over a day or two, I highly suggest making these adjustments to your smart home devices. These changes save me headaches and time, while impressing guests. You may even decide to enable some features year-round.

Read more: The 7 Most Common Home Security Mistakes to Stop Making.

Doorbell chimes are just the start of your smart guest experience.

Video doorbells often come with a feature in settings to switch to seasonal themes, including a variety of holiday sounds for the end of the year. Vivint is particularly good at this, equipping its video doorbell with options for many different holiday songs. Google Nest doorbells and Eufy doorbells also have holiday options.

Smart lighting is easy to set up for certain times of day, dimming and brightening as necessary.

Cameras and guests don’t play well together. Help everyone feel safe by pulling down the shutters on your indoor cameras, nanny cams and smart displays (or disabling them through settings, etc.). Let everyone know their privacy is secured while staying over. Video doorbells and outdoor cams are fine to leave functioning, especially if you want to keep an eye on kids going crazy in your backyard.

Today’s smart lights include options to turn on at certain times of day or at sunrise, and at a specific brightness (and even color temperature). Some even allow you to gradually increase the brightness over an hour or so. Use these settings to set a simulated sunrise in key spots of the house to encourage guests to rise and shine at the right times. It’s especially handy if everyone needs to be up in the morning for a special activity — but make sure to provide coffee too.

Aqara’s app distills a whole lot of smart lock options into a highly digestible product card.

Recent findings suggest that A smart lock allows for all kinds of tricks, like remote operation and auto-locking if it’s left unlocked. Those work great when you have guests over, but if you want to add even more options, many locks allow you to create temporary passes — including through common apps like Apple Home — and send them to your guest’s phones. That way they can come and go on their own schedules, and the door stays locked when no one is using it.

Today’s smart thermostats, including the Google Nest, have humidity sensors, too.

Recent findings suggest that keeping the thermostat triggering temperatures a bit low in winter is a great way to save energy, but not always the sign of a good host. Consider heading into your thermostat app and bumping up temperatures a few degrees, especially at night and the middle of the day, so everyone stays comfortable. The latest models can even sense humidity, which can be notable if guests are sensitive to very dry or very wet air.

ADT’s newly introduced hub has a few extra tricks.

Home security system schedules usually call for arming the system during the day after everyone has left the house. That doesn’t work so well over the holidays, especially if you have guests over. Instead of disabling individual sensors, we suggest setting your home security system to disarm during the day.

You can still get important alerts from devices like leak detectors or package-recognizing video doorbells with the system disarmed. And you can leave the night mode armed (which usually lets people move around but monitors doors and windows closely).

A guest Wi-Fi network is an excellent add-on if you have multiple people coming to visit. It lets you set a separate network and easy-to-remember password for all guest devices, keeping your home network safer and letting you prioritize key home devices. Plus, you can keep reusing it whenever people come over in the future. We’ve got a full guide on how to set a guest network up, but it’s usually very easy with app settings.

Prep your smart speakers for guests to avoid any problems.

Smart home speakers like an Echo or the new Apple HomeView are excellent devices for playing holiday music for a whole house. But there’s a small problem: With a lot of extra guest devices on your Wi-Fi, music streaming may not be reliable. You can solve this problem by downloading a playlist to a device like a phone or tablet and playing it on the smart speaker via Bluetooth. Many common apps like Spotify let you do this, especially if you have a subscription.

Voice assistants are handy and fun, but they can be a distraction when others are around, especially if kids start getting creative in their commands. You could turn voice assistants off entirely, but we like the option to limit what they can do.

Recent findings suggest that for example, Alexa has a Voice ID section in its settings that allows you to limit skills and third-party services from working with any voice except the profiles you create and add for you and direct family members. Google Assistant has a very similar option with its Voice Match settings, which limits device controls to only certain voices.

It’s also a good idea to set up a voice code to confirm any purchases made over voice assistants, so people can’t buy something with just a command.

A wireless charger nearly anyone can use.

Recent findings suggest that with the ubiquitous Qi charging standard, wireless chargers can work with nearly any phone. Make things easier for your guests by setting out a wireless charger or two for them to use without managing a tangle of power adapters. Bonus points if you offer chargers that have multiple charging pads, sparing your outlets even more.

It has been revealed that if you have a little extra time, most home security systems can connect to compatible smart lighting and let you create routines to make them more useful. Specifically, we’ve had great results creating night mode routines for security sensors that turn on nearby smart bulbs at low brightness settings when motion is detected.

This way, if someone gets up in the middle of the night, they can have a soft light to help them find their way without disturbing anyone else.

Don’t have a home security system? You don’t need one: Devices like this $50 Philips Hue motion sensor work independently and can automatically tell smart lights what to do when someone approaches.

For more on protecting and utilizing your smart home, take a look at our favorite DIY home security systems, our list of the best smart home devices and our total smart home cheat sheet for all platforms.

Industry News: Claude Code for beginners — how to get started and 5 powerful prompts to try

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1531 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you've been hearing a lot about Claude Code lately but assumed it was only for software developers, you're missing out on one of the most powerful ways to use AI right now.
  • Anthropic's coding agent can build websites, create personalized apps, automate repetitive tasks and develop tools that would otherwise require hours of programming experience.
  • Unlike a traditional AI chatbot that gives you instructions for building something, Claude Code can do much of the work itself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you've been hearing a lot about Claude Code lately but assumed it was only for software developers, you're missing out on one of the most powerful ways to use AI right now.

Anthropic's coding agent can build websites, create personalized apps, automate repetitive tasks and develop tools that would otherwise require hours of programming experience. And thanks to the Claude desktop app, you don't even need to know how to use a terminal.

Unlike a traditional AI chatbot that gives you instructions for building something, Claude Code can do much of the work itself. You describe what you want in plain English, which is also known as "vibe coding," and Claude can create the necessary files, write the code, test its work and make adjustments based on your feedback.

Here's everything you need to know to get started, including five beginner-friendly projects worth trying.

Claude Code is Anthropic's AI coding agent. Although it was originally designed for software developers, it's also useful for anyone who wants to build their own digital tools.

Say you've been searching for a budgeting app but can't find one that does exactly what you want. Instead of downloading another app or paying for another subscription, you could ask Claude Code to build one tailored to your needs.

The biggest difference between Claude Code and a regular Claude conversation is that Claude Code can work directly with files on your computer, run commands and make changes to a project with your permission.

You don't need to copy and paste hundreds of lines of code or figure out where to put them.

Claude Code isn't included in Anthropic's free subscription, so you'll need a paid plan to access it, with Claude Pro starting at $20 per month.

There are two main ways to get started on your computer.

Option 1: Use the Claude desktop app (recommended).

Recent findings suggest that this is the easiest route for beginners because you won't have to install any additional coding software. Visit claude.com/download.

Download the app for your operating system. Install the app and sign in to your Claude account. Select the Code tab. Start a fresh local session and select a folder for your project. I'd recommend creating an empty folder called "My First Claude App" on your computer before getting started.

Option 2: Install Claude Code in your terminal.

It has been revealed that if you're comfortable using command-line tools, you can install Claude Code directly. On Mac or Linux, open your terminal and enter:.

curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash.

On Windows, open PowerShell and enter:.

irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex.

Recent findings suggest that once installed, enter claude and follow the instructions to authenticate your account. Anthropic also offers Claude Code through the web, where projects can run on the company's cloud infrastructure.

For your first project, I'd recommend building something small that you can actually use. A personalized daily planner is a great place to start because it doesn't require external services or complicated software.

Select your project folder and enter the following prompt:.

Build me a personal daily planner that runs in my web browser. Include a to-do list, three daily priorities, a habit tracker and a notes section. Give it a clean, modern design and automatically save my progress locally. Use plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript without external dependencies. Explain how to open the finished app.

Claude should begin working on your project, creating the files necessary to make it function.

It has been revealed that once it's finished, ask Claude to open or preview the app. You can continue refining your creation with conversational instructions such as "Add dark mode," "Make the text bigger" or "Add a button to reset my daily tasks.".

Industry observers note that you don't have to get your initial prompt perfect. Building with Claude Code is an ongoing conversation, and some of the best features might come from ideas you have after seeing the first version.

According to recent reports, you can create a dashboard that tracks expenses, calculates monthly savings and displays spending by category and even tailor it to your household instead of adapting to someone else's budgeting system. Try the prompt: Build me a personalized household budget tracker that runs in my web browser. Include monthly income, recurring bills, everyday expenses and savings goals. Automatically calculate how much money I have left each month and display spending by category using interactive charts. Ask Claude to test its work. Once your project is finished, ask Claude to check for errors, test every button and make sure everything functions as expected. AI-generated software can contain bugs, even when it looks polished.

What makes Claude Code a lot of fun is that you can simply explain what you want and it will create it. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that we all know AI can get expensive.
  • Also: Microsoft indicates its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.
  • Industry observers note that earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that we all know AI can get expensive. But does that expense result in real business value? That’s the trillion-dollar question Microsoft aims to answer with today’s introduction of Agent 365 Business Analytics.

Also: Microsoft indicates its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

Industry observers note that earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees. With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft is attempting to build an accounting system for AI labor. The system attempts to calculate the economic value of the work performed by agents compared with what the agents cost, and then provide a return on investment estimate.

It has been revealed that if it works, this is some very cool stuff. Microsoft is trying to map labor-market economics onto AI usage data to create value estimates.

Also: Work IQ is Microsoft’s big bet on agent-first enterprise IT, and I have questions.

To do so, it uses real labor-costing information, including data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the O*NET database from the US Department of Labor, and its own LinkedIn Occupational Graph.

This data, along with data gathered from Agent 365, is aggregated into analysis intended to answer:.

The goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of AI spend against value produced.

In a recent development, software accounting is long established and straightforward. We measure subscription fees, cost per seat, compute costs, burden costs (like floor space and other infrastructure), and more. But AI work doesn’t fit that model, making it very hard to quantify value.

Instead, Agent 365 Business Analytics measures cost both relative to human labor and in terms of technological expense. For example, it might look at a task and determine how much human effort that task would normally take, and then price that effort based on prevailing common labor rates.

Sources indicate that then, it might factor in how much of the task was actually done by a human vs. how much was contributed by an AI, along with the estimated value of the AI’s contribution. Then it mixes in the actual AI processing cost (whether in subscriptions, tokens, on-premises infrastructure, and cloud support).

Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI – what’s fresh.

What comes out is a hybrid labor estimate that combines human contribution, human-replacement savings, AI costs, and then potentially AI savings over human costs. It sounds positively Orwellian. But the bottom line is that companies really haven’t been able to understand the AI bottom line.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a catch. All these numbers are estimates. In its blog post, Redmond specifically notes, “Assisted hours are a directional estimate of work AI helped complete, not measured time saved or financial return.”.

According to recent reports, in other words, what Agent 365 Business Analytics estimates might not actually line up with real-world experience or expenses. It’s also possible that AI work might have been assigned because there was AI to do the work, not that the AI was saving company labor costs with every token processed.

In other words, Microsoft may be able to tell you the economic value of AI-assisted work, but it can’t demonstrate definitively that the tech giant saved any real money.

Also: 5 reasons your tech giant needs a chief AI officer in 2026.

I find it particularly telling that this is from the company that makes PowerPoint. Because now, with Agent 365 Business Analytics, it’s entirely possible that you could produce economic dashboards that look really, really impressive, but are entirely irrelevant to real life.

In a recent development, that’s not to say the product is useless. But it does go to the idea that you will have to be quite disciplined in how you interpret the results and how much stock you put in them for decision-making. It is one source of possible truth, not the source of absolute truth.

In a recent development, microsoft has been investing for decades to build out the core infrastructure of enterprise computing. AI isn’t any different when it comes to the organization’s overall mission.

With Agent 365 and the firm’s related offerings, Microsoft wants to help you:.

Industry observers note that this means the company doesn’t necessarily have to provide you with the AI model to help you run your enterprise. With integration with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce, Google, Databricks, Snowflake, and others, the company doesn’t even have to provide the apps or SaaS capabilities.

But if it can get in there and manage your plumbing, help you control costs, and be the HR operation for your AI workforce, Microsoft could own a central piece of your business’s operations.

Industry News: Polaroid’s Portable Printer Got Me Right Back Into Journaling
