💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.
  • According to recent reports, should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty?
  • Many owners responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.

According to recent reports, should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty? Or is it better to rely on the severance payout to handle expenses?

Many owners responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.

For more ideas, I asked three financial experts how to manage money in the immediate aftermath of job loss.

It has been revealed that while it’s tempting to make quick decisions about tapping into a retirement fund or selling a house, it’s better to wait on any significant moves, states Parker Wine, retirement planning advisor at the financial firm Daniel A. White & Associates in Lewes, Delaware.

That’s because you need time to digest the situation and weigh the pros and cons of different options, he states. “People can get impulsive and panic, and it’s usually a bad thing to make decisions when you’re panicking,” he says.

Take your time, get second opinions and think through all of your options first, Wine suggests.

If you’re fortunate enough to receive a severance package, wait to sign it until you’ve reviewed it carefully and understand all of the details, says John Rafferty, partner and investment advisor representative at Solomon Financial in Carmel, Indiana.

For example, make sure you know about your health insurance options, such as whether you’ll receive insurance through COBRA or need to take out a latest policy in the health insurance marketplace.

Filing for unemployment and checking into any other available workplace benefits — such as help with your fresh job search — is also an vital part of understanding what support to expect in the weeks and months ahead, Rafferty adds.

Creating a bare-bones budget stripped of “extras” like restaurant meals or travel can help the severance payment last as long as possible, Rafferty notes.

“Now that you don’t have income coming in, ask yourself, ‘How much can I spend and where?’”.

You might be able to cut back on entertainment costs, coffee runs and clothing purchases, for example.

Industry observers note that at the same time, it’s notable to prioritize the essentials like mortgage payments, rent, utilities and food. Rafferty recommends calling your mortgage organization, utilities provider and any other lenders to ask if they have a hardship program for those experiencing financial challenges.

Opting in could give you more time to pay your bills or temporarily lower payments.

Industry observers note that it’s hard to stick to a budget that eliminates all entertainment, so Rafferty suggests finding enjoyable activities that come with a low price tag. Hiking, discovering a new park and participating in free community events are all ways to enjoy downtime on a budget.

“Having that release is mentally a massive thing so you can stay prepared for the job search,” he says. “Otherwise, it’s easy to get down and feel negative, and we need things to help us feel positive.”.

Similarly, connecting with friends and family during this time is crucial, indicates Laura Adams, accredited financial counselor and financial coach in Wilmington, North Carolina.

People often feel a sense of shame or embarrassment after job loss, and Adams encourages people to talk about their feelings and ask for help if needed. “Financial shame can cause us to make emotional rather than confident financial decisions,” she notes.

Sources indicate that starting some kind of side hustle to bring in extra cash can also help bridge the gap between the job loss and your next job, Wine indicates. Substitute teaching, working at a local public golf course and driving for a rideshare service are all options he’s seen people try.

Doing something latest also helps stave off boredom while unemployed, but he cautions that you’ll still owe taxes on any side income you bring in, so proposal accordingly.

In a recent development, all three financial experts also emphasized that a job loss is easier to handle with an emergency savings fund you can turn to, and suggested building one up — ideally three to six months’ worth of expenses. But starting small helps, too — while employed, if possible.

Recent findings suggest that the Redditor who posted the question mentioned that, like many Americans, they lacked emergency savings. This added urgency to the question of what to prioritize.

Sources indicate that reddit is an online forum where consumers share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like how to deal with job loss, so we sifted through Reddit forums to get a pulse check. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

New Hyundai Elantra Hybrid Debuts With 53 Mpg, AI in the Dash

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hyundai pulled back the cover on the upcoming 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class.
  • Recent findings suggest that the humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand.
  • Recent findings suggest that the updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai pulled back the cover on the upcoming 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class. The bold styling may not be for everyone — though, personally, I dig it — but economy car shoppers will certainly be interested in the compact hybrid sedan’s targeted 53 mpg and Gleo, Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that controls the automaker’s new Android Automotive OS-based dashboard tech.

Recent findings suggest that the humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand. It’s the automaker’s second-bestselling vehicle, behind only the Tucson. More importantly, the Elantra is one of the stalwarts of the affordable compact sedan class, a segment that many US automakers have abandoned in favor of more profitable SUVs. At a time when buyers are more sensitive than ever to inflated fuel costs and sticker prices, economy car options like the Elantra and its second-generation hybrid powertrain are worth our attention.

Recent findings suggest that the updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox. Combined output at the front wheels rises to 155 horsepower (up from 139 hp in the current car), thanks to a more powerful 45-kilowatt electric-assist motor (up from 32kW).

In a recent development, an updated regenerative braking system recaptures energy when slowing and now offers an “EV-like one-pedal driving experience” that can bring the car to a complete stop at its maximum setting. Additionally, the hybrid now features a latest Stay mode that lets the climate control and infotainment systems run while parked for up to 30 minutes without firing up the gas engine.

Sharing the stage in LA, the latest nonhybrid Elantra arrives with the same 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and continuously variable transmission as the current generation. At 147 hp with a target of 35 mpg combined, it’s no more powerful than before, but it should also be no less efficient, despite the sedan’s increased size. I’d say the hybrid is the better choice, though it will likely also be the more expensive powertrain option.

Recent findings suggest that inside, a new cockpit design moves the now-hoodless digital instrument cluster, a 9.9-inch “Slim Information Display,” away from the driver and toward the windshield on the dashboard. The new placement, similar to what I’ve seen on recent Toyota models, puts vehicle information closer to the driver’s line of sight.

It has been revealed that pleos Connect, Hyundai’s new Android Automotive OS-based infotainment suite, lives on a 12.9-inch center display. Despite being based on Android, it still features the automaker’s bespoke navigation and media software, rather than Google Maps. The system is remarked to be over-the-air updatable and features standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto for drivers who’d rather bring their own apps on the road.

In a recent development, the Pleos dashboard OS is matched with Gleo AI (who names these things?!), which is Hyundai’s newly introduced AI voice assistant that lets drivers and passengers talk to the car rather than occupy a hand on the touchscreen. Hyundai claims the system features “contextual language support, multi-command capability and zone-specific recognition,” which basically means the car knows who’s talking to it and which seat they’re in and can assign context to voice prompts based on the situation.

In a recent development, “Affordable doesn’t have to be anonymous,” remarked Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai’s senior vice president of product, at the unveiling. I agree: Hyundai’s designers clearly aren’t afraid to push the design envelope, and the latest Elantra is anything but bland.

Recent findings suggest that the sedan introduces the automaker’s Art of Steel design language, with chunky flared fenders that feel inspired by the brand’s recent latest SUVs. The tall greenhouse looks a bit cartoonish if you catch it at the wrong angle, but it provides increased headroom inside. From certain angles, the sedan’s beefy fenders remind me of an angular Korean take on the Subaru WRX. From other viewpoints, I can see inspiration from Hyundai’s N Vision 74 concept and the hydrogen-fueled Nexo, particularly in the triangular rear windows.

The sedan measures 188.8 inches bumper-to-bumper on a 108.3-inch wheelbase that is 1.2 inches longer than the current model’s. Hyundai notes the stretch for this generation improves rear-passenger space, now rated at 39.1 inches of legroom on the second row. The Elantra, according to its designers, now approaches the interior volume of a midsize car, a claim I’d take with a grain of salt had I not watched multiple six-foot-plus attendees slip into the back seat with relative ease.

It has been revealed that hyundai did not announce pricing or detailed specs at the auto show debut, and availability is still vague. However, based on the stated model years, which are usually slightly offset from calendar years, I expect the 2027 Elantra sedan to arrive in early 2027, with the 2028 Elantra Hybrid following in late 2027.

The NYT Connections puzzle today is not too difficult if you always put in your two cents.

Connections is the one of the most popular New York Times word games that's captured the public's attention. The game is all about finding the "common threads between words." And just like Wordle, Connections resets after midnight and each new set of words gets trickier and trickier—so we've served up some hints and tips to get you over the hurdle.

If you just want to be told today's puzzle, you can jump to the end of this article for today's Connections solution. But if you'd rather solve it yourself, keep reading for some clues, tips, and strategies to assist you.

According to recent reports, the NYT's latest daily word game has become a social media hit. The Times credits associate puzzle editor Wyna Liu with helping to create the new word game and bringing it to the publications' Games section. Connections can be played on both web browsers and mobile devices and require players to group four words that share something in common.

Each puzzle features 16 words and each grouping of words is split into four categories. These sets could comprise of anything from book titles, software, country names, etc. Even though multiple words will seem like they fit together, there's only one correct answer.

In a recent development, if a player gets all four words in a set correct, those words are removed from the board. Guess wrong and it counts as a mistake—players get up to four mistakes until the game ends.

According to recent reports, players can also rearrange and shuffle the board to make spotting connections easier. Additionally, each group is color-coded with yellow being the easiest, followed by green, blue, and purple. Like Wordle, you can share the results with your friends on social media.

Want a hint about the categories without being told the categories? Then give these a try:.

According to recent reports, need a little extra help? Today's connections fall into the following categories:.

Green: Interjections before a reaction.

Ready for the answers? This is your last chance to turn back and solve today's puzzle before we reveal the solutions.

Multitude: HOST, MASS, SEA, SLEW.

Interjections before a reaction: GEE, SAY, WELL, WHY.

Bubble __: BATH, GUM, TEA, WRAP.

Homophones of pronouns: EWE, EYE, HEE, WEE.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that korean luxury automaker Genesis launched its first hybrid models this week, debuting upcoming powertrains for the G80 sedan and GV80 SUV at the 2026 LA Auto Show.
  • Recent findings suggest that the hybridized versions of the brand’s most popular sedan and SUV arrive as American drivers show growing interest in energy-efficient cars, both battery electrics and hybrids, driven by high fuel costs and better understanding of the technologies.
  • The G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid share a 2.5-liter turbocharged hybrid powertrain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that korean luxury automaker Genesis launched its first hybrid models this week, debuting upcoming powertrains for the G80 sedan and GV80 SUV at the 2026 LA Auto Show. The firm says the electrified system is both more efficient and more powerful than the current nonhybrid versions. For buyers who want a more battery-focused experience, Genesis teased an upcoming 640-mile extended-range electric vehicle due to arrive in early 2027.

Recent findings suggest that the hybridized versions of the brand’s most popular sedan and SUV arrive as American drivers show growing interest in energy-efficient cars, both battery electrics and hybrids, driven by high fuel costs and better understanding of the technologies. Hybrids, in particular, have attracted attention because they behave like traditional combustion cars: There’s no need to install home charging hardware or change familiar driving and refueling habits. Just get in and reap better fuel economy with every mile.

The G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid share a 2.5-liter turbocharged hybrid powertrain. Genesis indicates the system is 16% more powerful than the gasoline-only version, outputting 347 horsepower and 391 pound-feet of torque. A new liquid-cooled battery pack improves thermal management and allows higher maximum discharge than Hyundai Motor Group’s previous air-cooled hybrid batteries, boosting performance. Both models use a seven-speed automatic transmission adapted to work with the electric motor’s regenerative braking.

According to recent reports, genesis hasn’t announced official fuel economy estimates, but claims the G80 Hybrid is 30% more efficient than the standard model, while the GV80 Hybrid is 24% more efficient. Based on current EPA figures, my math puts them in the ballpark of 30 mpg and 27 mpg, respectively. Any improvement is good, but those aren’t exactly earth-shattering gains. We’ll have to wait for the official ratings to be sure.

Each hybrid can be toggled into a silent EV mode for short distances — good for gliding into a driveway, garage or parking deck without waking the neighbors. However, without a plug, all the energy in the battery ultimately comes from the gas tank.

It has been revealed that A new Stay Mode lets owners run the climate control and infotainment without starting the engine for around 30 minutes. I like to think of it as the “moment of zen in the driveway before you have to go inside and face responsibility” mode, or maybe the “eating lunch in your car” mode. It’s similar to Toyota’s My Room Mode on its hybrids.

Aside from the powertrain, the G80 and GV80 Hybrids are largely identical to their combustion counterparts. Hybrid-specific touches include a three-dimensional G-Matrix grille inlay redesigned for these models, as well as upcoming exterior colors.

Inside, a 27-inch OLED display combining the instrument cluster and navigation stretches halfway across the dashboard. Tech features include Digital Key 2 Premium, which lets owners use their phone instead of a key fob to unlock and start the car, and active road noise cancellation. Genesis’ driver-assistance suite is headlined by the Highway Drive Assist 2 steering assistance system and the Remote Smart Parking Assist 2, which enables automatic parking with the driver inside or just nearby the car.

Prices for the sedan and SUV haven’t been announced. Final specifications and EPA fuel economy figures are expected closer to the early 2027 launch window.

My cynical side says that these upcoming models are just Genesis doing what Toyota has done since the RX 400h debuted in 2004. (To be fair, Genesis didn’t become an independent brand until 2015, so its rival has a bit of a head start.) In practical terms, the move brings Hyundai Motor Group’s luxury brand into parity with other group members and luxury car competitors that have rolled out updated hybrids over the last year, and meets customers’ increasing demand for more energy-efficient cars where they are.

In addition to its first hybrid sedan and SUV, Genesis executives revealed that the brand will expand the availability of its wild-styled, high-performance GV60 Magma full-electric SUV to more states and markets to meet higher-than-expected demand.

It has been revealed that at the debut event in LA, the brand also teased an upcoming extended-range EV — an EV with an onboard gasoline generator, essentially a very advanced plug-in hybrid — set to launch in early 2027. The EREV model is targeting over 640 miles before its “all-newly introduced high-performance battery” and gas tank both run dry, but Genesis didn’t give further details about the upcoming model.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s a tall order for an actor to embody any living person, but especially someone whom audiences may already have negative feelings about.
  • Rather than daunting, that challenge was “exciting” to actor Andrew Garfield, who plays OpenAI’s polarizing CEO Sam Altman in the film Artificial, slated for an initial Dec.
  • According to recent reports, garfield’s perspective on Altman morphed as he worked to better understand him, the actor told me ahead of an early screening hosted by SFFilm in the heart of the city where the story is set.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a tall order for an actor to embody any living person, but especially someone whom audiences may already have negative feelings about.

Rather than daunting, that challenge was “exciting” to actor Andrew Garfield, who plays OpenAI’s polarizing CEO Sam Altman in the film Artificial, slated for an initial Dec. 25 release. The biopic follows the rise of OpenAI, focusing on Altman’s relationships — particularly with his cofounder Ilya Sutskever (Yura Borisov) — as he relentlessly pursues success amid Silicon Valley’s artificial intelligence power struggle.

According to recent reports, garfield’s perspective on Altman morphed as he worked to better understand him, the actor told me ahead of an early screening hosted by SFFilm in the heart of the city where the story is set. His mission as an actor is to get to the “central truths” of who a person is, he said, “and try to merge my soul with theirs. And like all of us, Sam has so many facets.”.

That includes physical traits. Garfield indicates he had to lose weight and change his gait and voice to try to match Altman’s. The semblance is striking. From his bouncy stride to his clipped, gravelly speech, Garfield effortlessly emulates the Altman we’ve seen in interviews and Congressional testimonies. It’s a remarkable transformation — down to the sly, coaxing glint in his eyes — showcasing the breadth of Garfield’s acting talent.

It has been revealed that but it goes beyond physicality. Garfield had to dig deep internally to find elements “that felt like they were a match” with Altman, he noted. The result is an astonishingly believable portrayal of a multidimensional figure, at once pensive and inscrutable.

“There is a responsibility,” Garfield told me. “I take it very, very seriously to play any character, but particularly someone who’s alive, someone who’s pretty much my age. But also, maybe the greater responsibility is making sure that we interrogate these human beings that are leading our world into the next chapter, it seems.”.

“And it feels like our job as storytellers to reflect the times we’re in,” he added, “and no better way of doing that than by looking at the human beings — their personal relationships, their souls, all the diamond facets of their souls — and interrogate the people that have the power over our culture right now.”.

Artificial explores OpenAI’s rise through a rather bleak lens, with questions of moral responsibility and safety looming over the protagonists as they navigate the manufacturer’s success. The film is laced with dark satire, which offers moments of levity amid otherwise weighty meditations on the technology’s long-term impact.

According to recent reports, in one scene, when Sutskever is asked about the difference between AI and artificial general intelligence, which can theoretically match or even surpass human ability, he plainly responds, “It’s like how rocket ships are different from scooters.” He goes on to tell his cohorts that this is achievable “in your lifetime — well, maybe not yours or yours or yours,” as he points to the less youthful figures in the room. Moments like these elicited generous laughter from the audience.

Sources indicate that director Luca Guadagnino, known for deeply character-driven stories, such as Challengers and Call Me by Your Name, said he was following the news about Sam Altman’s temporary ousting from OpenAI in 2023 and was fascinated by the “Shakespearean feud” leading to that moment. Guadagnino applies his signature character-centric approach to OpenAI’s story, relying on slow, measured beats, piercing close-ups and suspenseful music to relay the stakes of each pivotal moment.

Industry observers note that “It’s never about the object; it’s always about the people,” Guadagnino remarked during a panel discussion after the screening. “It’s not about AGI or AI. It’s about the conflict between worldview and way of being, embodied by people that clash or fight for the vision they have.”.

He also said, “The point for me was more about trying to understand: How did the possibility of an incredible technology that can help all of us turn into the opportunity to get power in your hands and to become self-entitled?”.

In a recent development, garfield is no stranger to portraying prominent figures in the tech world, having played Eduardo Saverin, Facebook’s co-founder and former chief financial officer, in 2010’s The Social Network. On the surface, Artificial seems like a spiritual successor, recounting another defining moment in the tech industry. But the films differ in both tone and approach, with Artificial trading rapid-fire drama for a darker, more existential theme that occasionally ventures into more technical territory. What the films do share is a focus on bold, forceful personalities.

According to recent reports, “From that experience, I suppose, I was very curious about what it takes to win in this particular late-stage capitalist world that we’re in with these emerging technologies,” Garfield noted during the panel discussion. “What does it take to hold Sauron’s Ring of Power and not be completely burnt up by it? Is it possible to not completely lose yourself to that overwhelming, exponentially growing possibility and power?”.

According to recent reports, comic relief also arrives in the form of Ike Barinholtz playing OpenAI cofounder and tech mogul Elon Musk. By portraying him as a brutish, aloof figure who saunters in and out of rooms on a whim, he effectively underscores the absurdity of perceived importance and status. Almost every on-screen moment generated a murmur of laughter in the audience.

It has been revealed that “I think we’re all fascinated by these cultural, iconic figures who are leading us into this next stage of culture and society,” Garfield told the crowd. “They’re kind of kids. They’re kind of slightly stuck in an early developmental place, and that felt like a really notable part of Luca’s telling of this story.”.

In fact, he added, “[Guadagnino] would say to us, ‘This is a John Hughes movie. This is a high school, screwball comedy, just with slightly higher stakes — mixed in with a little bit of Invasion of the Body Snatchers.’ A very important part of this is that these are all kind of adolescent, high-school-minded people.”.

Even the way Garfield portrays Altman flippantly perching on couches and sitting cross-legged on tabletops while donning sunglasses — including during serious conversations about the future of OpenAI — was deeply researched.

In a recent development, “We had amazing consultants and researchers that work with us that gave us lots of information that’s not quite in the public arena about our characters,” Garfield said. “And Sam is someone who apparently would always sit like he was crisscross applesauce at play school, nursery school [or] kindergarten.”.

It has been revealed that ultimately, Artificial poses an open question about where society is headed and whether those at the helm are equipped to lead the charge. Amid weighty explorations of AI’s ramifications, the film paints a haunting, revelatory portrait of the cunning, mercurial figures making decisions that shape our world.

For Garfield, this presented an opportunity to dive deep into a figure like Altman, who, despite his prominence, remains largely elusive in the public eye.

According to recent reports, “I just wanted to tell this story and actually uncover for myself, excavate for myself, who is this person?” Garfield told me. “I’m dying to understand this person, and I get to try to understand this person, maybe more than anyone else has ever really tried to. And it feels like a gift to me.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Full Moon is just around the corner, and tonight the Moon is looking almost completely illuminated. We're still in the Waxing Gibbous phase for now, but it won't be long before visibility hits 100%.

As of Sunday, Nov. 22, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 92% of its surface visible.

Recent findings suggest that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Vaporum and Serenitatis, as well as the Aristarchus Plateau. With binoculars, you'll also see the Apennine Mountains, the Gassendi Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 14 and 17 landing spots, and the Rima Ariadaeus.

The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

According to recent reports, according to NASA, the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a New Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again.

New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

Sources indicate that first Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

It has been revealed that waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you like playing daily word games like Wordle, then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine.

There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown.

An vital note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle.

With Mortgage Rates Rising, Should You Hibernate Until Spring?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.
  • It has been revealed that the average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov.
  • A mortgage is a substantial ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.

It has been revealed that the average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov. 19, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.) We calculate our weekly average using daily APRs recorded over the past five business days.

A mortgage is a substantial ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast. Say you’re borrowing $400,000 on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. Compared with last week, your monthly principal and interest payment would be about $78 higher today.

One bad week doesn't make a trend, but a jump like this can make putting your house hunt on hold until spring feel like a safer bet. So … is it?

Before deciding whether to buy a house now or wait, it helps to know what's pushing mortgage rates higher.

Right now, mortgage rates are still feeling the aftershocks from two major inflation reports last week. First, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) showed consumer prices rose more than expected in October. Then, the Producer Price Index (PPI) showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its biggest annual increase in nearly four years.

In a recent development, while CPI shows how prices have changed, PPI can offer clues about what's coming next. Faced with higher costs, businesses may raise their own prices to compensate, keeping inflation elevated. Federal Reserve policymakers aren't expecting much relief anytime soon, either. According to meeting minutes released Nov. 18, they expect inflation to remain elevated above their 2% target for a while.

According to recent reports, to cool rising prices, the Fed can raise the federal funds rate, which is the benchmark interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. A rate hike is widely expected at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.

Even after a Fed rate hike, there’s no telling how rapidly inflation will cool — or whether mortgage rates will follow. (Inflation is just one of many forces that affect mortgage rates, after all.) So if you do wait until spring to buy a house, don't do it just because you're betting on a cheaper mortgage.

If you're not in a rush to move, winter can be a good time to regroup. Fewer homes typically go up for sale from November through February, so waiting until spring could give you more options.

According to recent reports, but upcoming data from the National Association of Realtors suggests this year's slowdown goes beyond the usual seasonal lull. High mortgage rates and home prices are making it tough for many buyers to make the numbers work. For some buyers, waiting isn't a strategy — it's the only option.

Pending home sales, a measure of homes under contract, fell 16.7% in October compared with a year earlier, NAR reports. All four U.S. regions saw declines. At this rate, NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun warned that annual home sales could fall to their lowest level since the mid-1990s.

“Either sizable housing demand is building in the background, or the dream of homeownership is increasingly out of reach for many Americans,” Yun said in a news release.

Whether you're waiting by choice or necessity, you can use the time to strengthen your finances. Paying down debt, strengthening your credit score or saving for a bigger down payment could help you qualify for a better mortgage deal.

Every little bit helps when today’s mortgage rates are this high.

Mortgage preapprovals typically expire after 60 to 90 days. If you're already preapproved, why not keep an eye on listings this winter? (Hey, I’m an optimist. All it takes is one house.).

Think like a seller for a second. If you're listing your house in the dead of winter, you're probably not doing it just for fun. You might have a deadline, and you’re probably more willing to negotiate. In the winter, buyers have less competition — and more room to negotiate a lower price, closing cost credits or repairs. Those savings on the sticker price might help offset today's higher borrowing costs.

Spring typically brings more homes for sale, but it also brings more buyers competing for them. And if mortgage rates end up dropping this spring, you won't be the only one coming out of hibernation.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to reports from Italy, Liverpool are regularly scouting a red-hot striker who’s emerged as a shock candidate for the Golden Boot in Serie A this season.

    Andoni Iraola has been almost exclusively reliant on Alexander Isak at centre-forward since taking charge of the Reds in the summer, with Hugo Ekitike continuing his recovery from a long-term Achilles injury.

    The Frenchman is targeting a return to action next month (The Athletic), although it appears that Anfield chiefs are keeping tabs on a positional alternative who’s emerging as a breakthrough sensation in one of Europe’s major leagues.

    A report from Corriere dello Sport has claimed that Liverpool are sending scouts ‘every week’ to watch Gustavo Varela, who’s been in remarkable goalscoring form with Monza since joining the Serie A outfit in the summer.

    Napoli and Juventus have also been strongly linked with the 21-year-old, who’s been the subject of enquiries from Tottenham, Brentford and Sunderland, with the list of suitors growing in tandem with his goal return in the Italian top flight.

    Ivan Juric’s side reportedly want €40m (£33.5m) for the Portuguese hitman, which’d represent a monumental profit on a player they signed from Gil Vicente in July for a paltry €2.5m (£2.1m).

    (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

    Sources indicate that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    Varela is at the moment the leading scorer in Serie A this season with nine goals, which is remarkable when his team are currently in the relegation zone, and he accounts for more than half of their goal tally in the top flight so far.

    For someone who’d scored just seven times in 34 senior appearances before the summer, his form since joining Monza has been extraordinary. Should that continue, it’s safe to say that he won’t be at the Stadio Brianteo for much longer.

    What Liverpool would need to consider is whether this is a mere purple patch from the Portuguese youngster, or the start of a journey towards being one of Europe’s most feared centre-forwards.

    Varela has scored nine Serie A goals from an xG of just 5.48 (Fotmob), an astonishing overperformance which begs the question as to whether he can maintain that for a full campaign.

    If Isak keeps up his own hot streak and Ekitike gets back to the levels he’d shown prior to his injury, it’d be difficult to see the Monza striker getting much of a look-in at Anfield.

    However, it’s easy to see why Liverpool are routinely dispatching scouts to gather information on one of the breakout stars of European football in 2026.

    • According to recent reports, the U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Courtney Carlsen – Nov 22, 2026 at 5:30PM EST.

    Rare-earth elements are key ingredients in high-strength permanent magnets that enable many of today's modern electronics, clean energy technologies, and defense applications, including drones and precision-guided munitions.

    The United States is taking steps to create a domestically controlled "mine-to-magnet" supply chain as it looks to reduce its dependence on China, which controls 70% of rare-earth extraction and 90% of processing, according to a research report from The Motley Fool.

    According to recent reports, the U.S. government is pouring money into rebuilding a rare-earth supply chain, and USA Rare Earth (USAR -8.73%) is one company playing a key role in unlocking America's rare-earth industry. The company made several acquisitions to hit the ground running. But over the next five years, developing the Round Top mine in Texas will be key to its long-term success.

    In recent years, the U.S. has taken a pivotal role in expanding the country's rare-earth supply chains by providing funds, investing in companies in the space, setting price floors, and acting as a guarantor to break China's stronghold.

    In June, the Department of Commerce finalized CHIPS Act funding of roughly $1.6 billion for USA Rare Earth, with $1.3 billion from senior secured loans and the remainder from grants.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    The funding supports its efforts to enter rare-earth mining and processing, including its acquisitions of Less Common Metals and Serra Verde Group, as well as the expansion of processing and magnet-making facilities in Oklahoma and South Carolina.

    In the coming years, USA Rare Earth will integrate its acquisitions, which help secure feedstock for rare-earth magnets while building out its U.S. manufacturing footprint. But a major part of its future lies in developing the Round Top deposit in West Texas.

    The Round Top deposit is rich in heavy rare-earth elements (HREEs), which no U.S. mines currently produce at commercial scale. This would give USA Rare Earth a massive HREE supply, complementing its Serra Verde mine in Brazil, the largest-scale producer of HREEs outside Asia.

    Industry observers note that by owning the mine, factories, and processing, USA Rare Earth can capture margins across the entire value chain. The next five years are crucial for USA Rare Earth, and developing the Round Top project is a massive undertaking projected to cost around $1.4 billion. The company doesn't expect to begin commercial production at the Round Top until late 2028, with full-scale production coming by 2030.

    Sources indicate that for investors seeking exposure to the U.S. rare-earth supply chain build-out, USA Rare Earth is a highly speculative, risky stock, especially as it incurs gigantic costs to integrate and expand its mine-to-magnet supply chain over the next several years.

    Breaking: This Oceanfront Hilton Resort in Florida Is Great for Groups

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1488 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hilton is making a major play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort.
    • In a recent development, the resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R.
    • Industry observers note that room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hilton is making a major play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

    In a recent development, the resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

    Industry observers note that room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

    Recent findings suggest that hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

    Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

    If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

    For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

    You can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

    Make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

    Recent findings suggest that for cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

    Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

    It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

    Stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

    Despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

    I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

    In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

    Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

    The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

    The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

    Even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

    This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

    Sources indicate that there are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

    According to recent reports, for breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

    It has been revealed that if you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

    The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

    For lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

    It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

    You can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

    For a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

    One of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

    I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

    If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

    Recent findings suggest that the family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

    I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

    I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

    If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

    Sources indicate that next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

    The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

    It has been revealed that one of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

    Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

    I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

    Industry observers note that if you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

    I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

    But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.47%) (BRKB -0.36%), under the direction of Warren Buffett, began buying Apple (AAPL -1.90%) shares in the first quarter of 2016.
    • Recent findings suggest that even after trimming the position from fourth-quarter 2023 through the end of 2025, as of Nov.
    • Here's what Berkshire holding on to the Apple stake tells investors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neil Patel – Nov 22, 2026 at 5:35PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Apple ›.

    Industry observers note that berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.47%) (BRKB -0.36%), under the direction of Warren Buffett, began buying Apple (AAPL -1.90%) shares in the first quarter of 2016. That investment has worked out extremely well. At one point, the Cupertino tech giant accounted for 50% of the conglomerate's portfolio.

    Recent findings suggest that even after trimming the position from fourth-quarter 2023 through the end of 2025, as of Nov. 17, the ”Magnificent Seven” stock represented 25% of Berkshire Hathaway's total public equity portfolio, and it is still its largest holding. The number of shares remained unchanged this year. This was despite there being a lot of shuffling among other positions.

    Here's what Berkshire holding on to the Apple stake tells investors.

    Sources indicate that over the three-month period from the start of July to the end of September, Apple shares traded at an average price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 36.8. Any rational investor would call this an expensive stock. That's doubly true for those who see equities through a value-focused lens. The share price has moved 29% higher in 2026.

    In a recent development, berkshire Hathaway didn't sell a single share during the third quarter. This might come as a surprise to those who have followed the diversified corporation's actions in recent years.

    Warren Buffett oversaw the selling of Apple shares over multiple quarters from the end of 2023 to the end of 2025. For example, during the second quarter of 2024, when the technology stock traded at an average P/E multiple of 29, much lower than what it sells for today, Berkshire Hathaway cut its position dramatically.

    While the single holding had become a significant part of the portfolio, it's fair to assume that valuation played a part in these decisions. Now, with a P/E ratio that's approaching 40, it looks like less emphasis is being placed on the valuation being an influential factor.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, greg Abel has been the chief executive officer of Berkshire Hathaway since the start of 2026. He has made notable moves in his short tenure thus far, but as outside observers, we have zero clue what he and Warren Buffett are discussing regarding the conglomerate's capital allocation strategy. All we can do is try to come up with some takeaways.

    Sources indicate that staying true to Warren Buffett's investing philosophy, the Apple position is a clear signal that Berkshire Hathaway will hold on to its winners and let them run. "When we own portions of outstanding businesses with outstanding managements, our favorite holding period is forever," Buffett wrote in his 1988 shareholder letter.

    Sources indicate that the iPhone maker has been in the portfolio for nearly 11 years. Given how much of the market is driven by short-term behavior these days, that time horizon seems like an eternity.

    It has been revealed that if Berkshire Hathaway did sell some of its Apple shares in Q3, it wouldn't know where to move that capital. This is a persistent problem. Compared to the hundreds of billions of dollars on the balance sheet that earn low yields, an expensive Apple stock still offers the potential for higher returns. This benefits Berkshire Hathaway shareholders.

    In a recent development, valuation should always be viewed separately from the underlying business. In this instance, Berkshire Hathaway's inactivity is a vote of confidence in the quality of Apple's operations.

    It's hard to dispute that the consumer tech juggernaut is one of the finest companies we've ever seen. A valuable brand, ongoing pricing power, customer loyalty, and innovative DNA are attractive traits. There's also its incredible financial performance, shown by a fiscal 2026 free cash flow margin of 28%.

    This isn't a sign for the average investor to go out and buy Apple stock. It is proof, however, that buying great businesses and leaving them alone can work wonders for your portfolio.

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 5:58PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Morningstar ›.

    Sources indicate that deciding between established financial research and high-growth payment technology requires a choice between steady market influence and rapid expansion. Is Morningstar (MORN -0.30%) or Sezzle (SEZL -6.09%) the better buy today?

    In a recent development, morningstar provides the critical research and data that power modern investment decisions for millions of retail and institutional people. Conversely, Sezzle is a disruptor in the payments space, offering flexible financing options for younger consumers. While both operate in the financial world, they cater to different market segments with unique risk and reward profiles.

    Sources indicate that morningstar sells investment insights, data, and technology tools to a massive audience, including roughly 4.2 million individual investors and 425,000 financial advisors. The company serves eight primary customer groups, ranging from retirement blueprint providers and wealth managers to asset managers and fixed-income security issuers. Recently, it has integrated artificial intelligence through partnerships with major technology firms to automate analytics and improve user experience.

    In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $2.6 billion, representing revenue growth of approximately 9.4%. This expansion helped the firm achieve net income of close to $445.5 million during the same period. The steady climb in both top and bottom lines suggests consistent demand for the company's proprietary financial data and research services.

    It has been revealed that as of its September 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 1.8x (or 1.6x excluding operating lease liabilities). This ratio, which compares total debt to shareholder equity, reflects an increase in financial leverage after the tech giant took on additional debt to fund acquisitions and share repurchases. The current ratio, which measures a company's ability to cover its short-term debts with short-term assets, is approximately 1.05x. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $492.8 million (following $442.6 million in fiscal year 2025).

    Sezzle operates a platform that allows consumers to finance purchases at the point of sale. It focuses heavily on Gen Z and Millennial shoppers, connecting them with a vast network of merchants to increase average order values. By integrating with e-commerce platforms, the company captures a growing slice of the fintech stocks landscape.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $581.6 million, marking significant revenue growth of nearly 38.9%. This surge in activity led to a net income of close to $182.6 million for the period. The company also maintained a strong net margin of roughly 31.4% during this high-growth phase, indicating it is generating significant profit from its revenue.

    As of its September 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio stands at approximately 4.2x, suggesting a robust ability to cover immediate liabilities. The debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.4x, meaning its total debt is less than half of its shareholder equity. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $297.6 million, providing the manufacturer with substantial capital to reinvest in its growth and fund share repurchases.

    Morningstar faces risks tied to its reputation, as any perceived conflict of interest in its credit ratings or research could damage its brand. Its business is sensitive to market volatility, which can reduce asset-based fees when total market values decline. The tech giant also competes with major data providers such as S&P Global (NYSE:SPGI) and MSCI (MSCI -2.22%) in the institutional research space.

    Sezzle relies heavily on a single originating bank partner, WebBank, for the majority of its loans, which creates a significant concentration risk. It faces intense competition in the payment sector and ongoing regulatory scrutiny regarding consumer lending practices and interest rates. Additionally, antitrust litigation involving partners like Shopify (SHOP -6.25%) could indirectly impact its growth trajectory or existing merchant relationships.

    Sources indicate that morningstar offers a more conservative entry point based on its sales, while Sezzle carries a higher premium that reflects its faster growth and superior net margin. The Forward P/E ratio compares a manufacturer's share price to its future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    But there are some risks that give me pause: Sezzle lends to shoppers, so bad loans matter. Its newest products start with higher losses, and regulators and a lawsuit against Shopify add costs and uncertainty.

    Morningstar, a trusted name in investing research, carries less credit risk, and its stock costs less relative to expected earnings. Its operating profit jumped last quarter, but sales growth is modest. Ultimately, I like that Sezzle is already profitable and still early in its expansion, with room to add new services. If you're investing for the long haul and can handle some risk, Sezzle's fast-growing payments platform looks like the better buy for 2027.

    • Recent findings suggest that upstart's (UPST -7.88%) days as a hot fintech stock have long since passed.
    • While shares in this artificial intelligence (AI) lending technology company have seen brief partial rebounds in recent years, I’m looking more closely at fintech names with stronger growth stories, namely SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%).
    • At first glance, it may seem illogical that Upstart continues to tumble.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Thomas Niel – Nov 22, 2026 at 6:04PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than SoFi Technologies ›.

    Recent findings suggest that upstart's (UPST -7.88%) days as a hot fintech stock have long since passed. It was trading near $400 per share back in 2021, but recently was changing hands for around $17 per share, a nearly 96% price decline.

    While shares in this artificial intelligence (AI) lending technology company have seen brief partial rebounds in recent years, I’m looking more closely at fintech names with stronger growth stories, namely SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%).

    At first glance, it may seem illogical that Upstart continues to tumble. After all, following steep revenue declines in 2023 and 2024, sales and earnings have improved dramatically. In 2024, revenue and earnings per share (EPS) came in at $628.8 million and -$1.44, respectively. In 2025, revenue surged to just over $1 billion, with diluted EPS at $0.45 per share, marking a massive swing back to profitability.

    For 2026, analysts' estimates call for Upstart to report $1.35 billion in sales and EPS of $1.84. Alas, there is a reason the market prices Upstart at such a low multiple to those estimates.

    According to recent reports, first, there is high uncertainty over future growth. Although the company recently reported a 34% increase in quarterly revenue to $371 million, and diluted earnings of $0.33 per share, up 43.4% from the prior year's quarter, management walked back its full-year guidance. Previously estimating  $1.4 billion in revenue and adjusted EBITDA of $294 million, Upstart's full-year 2026 outlook now calls for $1.32 billion in revenue and adjusted EBITDA of $260 million.

    Second, the recent pullback in AI stocks and tech stocks has likely intensified the situation. This sell-off has spilled over into the fintech space, including shares in SoFi, a company more richly priced than Upstart but with far greater long-term upside potential.

    Like Upstart, SoFi has recently reported strong growth. Last quarter, the digital-first financial services manufacturer reported net revenue of $1.4 billion, a 44% increase from the prior year's quarter. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 70% year over year, to $470 million. EPS came in at $0.18, a 63% increase from the $0.11 in diluted adjusted EPS reported for Q3 2025.

    Sources indicate that better yet, SoFi's management provided bullish guidance for the coming year. In 2027, the firm anticipates 27% adjusted net revenue growth and adjusted earnings of $0.90 per share, adding that it could achieve these goals without raising additional capital. With SoFi Technologies changing hands today at around $13.50 per share, the stock is trading at around 15 times next year's estimated earnings.

    In a recent development, longer-term, if SoFi can continue to grow at a moderate clip, steadily becoming a major "financial supermarket," shares could climb further, to past highs in the $30s per share, and beyond. Contrast that with Upstart, which, while still guiding for further growth, is revising that guidance downward. Worse yet, although both SoFi and Upstart are involved in the personal lending space, Upstart arguably has greater exposure. SoFi started as a lender but has since expanded into banking, brokerage, and other financial services, with its ability to cross-sell bolstering confidence in its growth story.

    That mentioned, it's still possible for Upstart to thrive while SoFi flounders. The sell-side remains divided on SoFi, perhaps reluctant to assign it a fintech valuation, given that it will eventually be classified as a bank stock. Upstart has tanked on poor guidance, but any sort of better-than-feared results and outlook could be enough to drive a relief rally. Nevertheless, if you're looking at either stock as a possible long-term investment rather than a trade, consider SoFi the better of the two.

    Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

    The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    Industry observers note that A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to fresh inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    It has been revealed that next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a big reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

    If PCE shows inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

    In a recent development, I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index revealed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

    Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you strategy to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

    Industry observers note that also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    • This is why you should always wait for evidence before trading on your thesis.
    • According to recent reports, back in June, I started rethinking my bearish outlook on artificial intelligence (AI) voice chatbot specialist SoundHound AI (SOUN -10.31%).
    • According to recent reports, since then, its stock has fallen 54%.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By John Bromels – Nov 22, 2026 at 6:50PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than SoundHound AI ›.

    This is why you should always wait for evidence before trading on your thesis.

    According to recent reports, back in June, I started rethinking my bearish outlook on artificial intelligence (AI) voice chatbot specialist SoundHound AI (SOUN -10.31%). I suggested investors should keep an eye on the company.

    According to recent reports, since then, its stock has fallen 54%. Over the past year, it's down 75%. Boy, am I glad I didn't recommend buying it in June!

    But at just $3.10 per share (at the time of this writing), has SoundHound's stock price dropped to the point that it's now a buy? It could be ... if SoundHound can make this one thing happen by 2027.

    According to recent reports, what's so strange about the stock's recent performance is that trailing-12-month (TTM) revenue has continued to rise even as the stock price has fallen. Q3 revenue hit a record $62.4 million, bringing TTM revenue to $223.6 million.

    Meanwhile, SoundHound's shares peaked in late 2024 at $24.23 per share. They're now sitting at about $3.10 per share, a 52-week low.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Management expects revenue to continue improving, with guidance of $350 million to $400 million for 2027. But there's more to that number than meets the eye.

    Recent findings suggest that soundHound is still digesting its recent acquisition of LivePerson, an enterprise digital messaging platform with significant debt on its balance sheet. SoundHound used an equity raise to retire that debt completely.

    Sources indicate that livePerson brought an extensive patent portfolio and existing contracts with major Fortune 100 companies. SoundHound is now integrating LivePerson's messaging infrastructure with its own OASYS agentic voice AI platform to offer an omnichannel customer engagement system that "operates natively across voice, web, mobile, SMS, and social channels.".

    Industry observers note that as if this transition weren't enough, SoundHound is also switching to a recurring-revenue, hosted-solution model. This kind of transition is usually a long-term positive for a organization, but can result in lumpy revenue during the transition period.

    Another variable is the high amount of churn among LivePerson customers prior to the acquisition. Plus, because the acquisition didn't close until Sept. 4, LivePerson only contributed about $14 million to SoundHound's Q3 revenue. That means SoundHound's organic revenue growth was just 15.2% year over year (YOY), which is much lower than Q2's 45% growth and Q1's 52% growth.

    For SoundHound to turn around its slumping stock price, it needs to show it can do more than just achieve revenue growth. It needs to make meaningful improvements in the quality of its revenue.

    In a recent development, cost reductions and synergies with LivePerson will play a role. Management believes it can identify $80 million in annualized cost reductions that will take effect by the end of the calendar year. But the company has also noted that it is exiting some legacy contracts with negative growth margins, which will result in the loss of some lower-quality revenue.

    Recent findings suggest that ultimately, SoundHound's 2027 revenue guidance implies 68% revenue growth from the past year. The LivePerson acquisition will likely get the company most of the way there. What investors should instead be watching is whether SoundHound's margins and quarterly cash burn improve, how much of its existing revenue is converting to annual recurring revenue, and how well it retains and upsells LivePerson's customer base.

    If SoundHound AI can show meaningful revenue quality improvement by 2027, it will look like a steal at its current share price.

    Arm vs. Marvell Technology: Which Artificial Intelligence Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
